tier_reason: mfoo/Math-Library-Test README times GLM 0.9.3.B against an Eigen 3 snapshot (and CML 1.0.2) with public code (src/Driver.cpp, src/Main.cpp, src/androidactivity.cpp) and CPU models, but no GCC or NDK version is given and the per-column flags are only partly derivable from CMakeLists.txt, so it falls short of A; it is an obscure 42-star hobby test, not a well-known suite, so not B.
notes: All claimed numbers match the README table exactly, and the record's caveats are accurate: Driver.cpp runs count=10 matrices (Main.cpp default and androidactivity.cpp testLibraries(10)) times NUM_TESTS=1,000,000, the non-SSE laptop column is -O0, and the Eigen generator sets only the diagonal while GLM 0.9.3 default-constructs identity. The GLM win holds only on the 2010 HTC Desire armeabi-v7a builds; on the SSE x86 build Eigen is 2.5x (additions) and 4.7x (multiplications) faster and the author chose Eigen, plain armeabi is a tie, and the versions tested are 14 years old. Metadata checked on github.com: 11.3k stars, not archived, latest release GLM 1.0.3 (2025-12-31), last commit 2026-04-07 (active); the repo states the Happy Bunny License or the MIT License (dual), so MIT/copyable stands. Math-Library-Test has no LICENSE file (404) but it is only the evidence repo.

tier_reason: fereidani/musl-vs-glibc publishes the harness (benchmark.c, run.sh), the compiler (zig 0.15.2 using clang 20.1.2), the full flag set in run.sh and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U), and its README table is the source of every claimed number, which meets A for a third-party run. The glibc version is not printed, but the kernel string (6.8.0-87-generic #88~22.04.1-Ubuntu) pins the host to Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35, an inference) and zig 0.15.2 pins the bundled musl.

corrections.claimed_speedup: glibc fastest in 17 of 32 rows (musl 2, musl+jemalloc 11, 2 ties); README summary: 'glibc wins most benchmarks'. ns/op, glibc vs musl: strncmp 9.91 vs 366.91; strcpy 22.05 vs 129.35; strncpy 25.20 vs 136.77; strstr_search 36.28 vs 104.23; strtod_parse 52.40 vs 226.72 (4.3x, derived from page data); regex_match 117.54 vs 694.23 (5.9x, derived from page data); qsort_int 214387.15 vs 591408.11 (2.8x, derived from page data); malloc_free_small 10.78 vs 122.61; malloc_free_medium 828.38 vs 3343.75. musl is faster on atoi_parse 3.96 vs 9.28, bsearch_int 10.52 vs 16.02, sprintf_float 136.34 vs 160.56, strtok_parse 5.71 vs 15.23, strtok_r_parse 4.94 vs 14.76, strrchr 157.31 vs 354.19 and memcpy 154.19 vs 4043.27; musl+jemalloc beats glibc on malloc_free_medium 80.59 vs 828.38 and malloc_free_small 10.15 vs 10.78.
corrections.caveats: Third-party hobby repo (7 stars, 7 commits, no licence file), one machine, one calibrated run per benchmark (250 ms target) with no repeats or variance; results dated 2025-11-18. The glibc version is not stated: the binary is built with zig cc -target x86_64-linux-gnu and runs against the host's dynamic glibc (kernel string 6.8.0-87-generic #88~22.04.1-Ubuntu, so Ubuntu 22.04 and probably glibc 2.35, an inference). The musl side is zig's bundled musl compiled by zig (its optimisation level not stated) and linked statically, so the two sides are built differently and glibc calls go through the PLT. Several rows are not meaningful: strlen, strcmp and memcmp show about 0.1 ns/op because the loop-invariant pure calls are hoisted out of the loop (ties); the strstr haystack is cut to about 16 KB because the strcpy that plants the first marker writes a NUL (benchmark.c), and the strstr averages look low for the 10 of 16 needles that scan that whole haystack (verifier's estimate, not reproduced). The memcpy row (glibc 4043.27 vs musl 154.19 ns for 16 KB, about 4 GB/s vs 106 GB/s) is not a harness artifact but matches glibc bug BZ 30994, 'REP MOVSB performance suffers from page aliasing' on AMD Zen 3/Zen 4 when (dst-src) mod 4096 is small (reported 4.2 GB/s vs 111 GB/s), addressed upstream by 'x86: Fix Zen3/Zen4 ERMS selection (BZ 30994)' (WebSearch snippets only; sourceware.org is blocked here), so results on this CPU depend on the glibc version. A vendor blog (BellSoft Alpaquita, which sells a musl build with tuned routines) reports glibc ahead of musl on memcpy and memcmp; the page was EGRESS_BLOCKED and its numbers are not used. repo_url is the read-only unofficial mirror (archived 2026-02-15, last commit 2026-01-20); upstream development is at sourceware.org, which was not opened. Baseline is a C library, not a C++ standard library.

notes: Every claimed number matches the README table; claimed_speedup now also lists the musl wins it omitted (sprintf_float, strtok_r_parse) and the musl+jemalloc malloc_free_small win. The memcpy row is explained by the known glibc rep movsb page-aliasing bug on AMD Zen (BZ 30994, snippet only), so the caveat no longer calls it a harness artifact; strlen/strcmp/memcmp rows are hoisted no-ops. maintenance_status left 'active': the bminor mirror was archived 2026-02-15 (strict rule would say abandoned), but glibc itself is the actively developed default libc and the mirror's last commit (2026-01-20) is within 12 months; metadata checked on github.com (1.9k stars, 487 forks, LGPL-2.1).
